I dug through the whole codebase, ran the build, the tests, and the type checker, and checked your deps and CI against upstream. Here's what I found.

## The short answer on your actual question

**There are no dependency upgrades to do.** `npm outdated` returns nothing, and spot-checks confirm it (react 19.2.8 is current). Your recent "Updated dependencies" commits did their job.

But dependency currency is exactly what bit you: **two things are broken in production right now, both from upstream changes.**

---

## P0 — Broken today

### 1. The AI command palette is dead

`src/server/ai.functions.ts:135` uses `groq("llama-3.1-8b-instant")`. Groq **shut that model down on August 16, 2026** — five days ago. Their recommended replacement is `openai/gpt-oss-20b`.

Worse, it fails silently: the `catch` at `ai.functions.ts:159` swallows the error into `"AI request failed. Try again."`, so there's no signal anything is wrong.

The fix is one string — I verified `'openai/gpt-oss-20b'` is already in `@ai-sdk/groq`'s `GroqChatModelId` union, so it's a drop-in. It's also faster (~1000 tps vs the old model) and cheap ($0.075/$0.30 per 1M). Two other spots need the same edit: the hardcoded `"llama-3.1"` label at `CommandAgent.tsx:554`, and I'd add a `console.error` + a distinguishable user message so the next shutdown isn't invisible.

### 2. `main` is red — deploys are blocked

Run `32480357913` (commit `9f33fb6`, "Updated dependencies") failed in 31s:

```
Error: vite-plus bundles vitest@4.1.10, but @vitest/coverage-v8@4.1.11 is installed.
```

I reproduced it locally. Your last dependency bump pushed vitest/coverage-v8 to 4.1.11, but `vite-plus@0.2.9` bundles 4.1.10. Three places need to agree: `devDependencies.vitest`, `devDependencies.@vitest/coverage-v8`, and `overrides.vitest` — all to `4.1.10`.

**Heads up before you fix it:** your coverage gate is currently inert and will start biting. `vite.config.ts:59` has `thresholds: { global: { branches: 70, ... } }`. In Vitest 4 the type is `Thresholds | ({[glob: string]: ...} & Thresholds)` — so `global` is parsed as a *glob pattern* matching zero files. The 70% gate has been enforcing nothing. Once coverage runs again with `thresholds: { branches: 70, functions: 70, lines: 70, statements: 70 }` at the top level, it will very likely fail: you have 17 tests covering `utils/` and `ToolCard`, while four route files and the 562-line `CommandAgent` are untested.

While you're in there: `overrides.vite: npm:@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core@0.2.8` is stale — `npm ls` resolves 0.2.9. Worth confirming it's still load-bearing at all.

---

## P1 — The architectural one

**This should be a static site, and isn't.** Three symptoms, one root cause:

**a) `/blog` ships every post's full HTML.** `fetchAllBlogPosts()` returns `BlogPost[]` including `html`, and the loader hands all of it to the hydration payload. Measured against your production build: **30,005 of the 46,082 bytes of `/blog` (65%) is the hydration payload**, most of it rendered article HTML the list page never displays. This grows linearly with every post you write. Minimum fix: a list DTO that omits `html`.

**b) A server round-trip for build-time-constant data.** The markdown is `import.meta.glob`'d at build time and never changes, yet `/blog` and `/blog/$slug` go through server functions on every client navigation.

**c) No robots.txt, sitemap.xml, or RSS** — all four SEO endpoints 404 on the live site. No `og:image` or canonical URL either. For a blog, RSS is a real miss.

The idiomatic TanStack Start answer covers all three:

```ts
tanstackStart({
  srcDirectory: "src",
  prerender: { enabled: true, crawlLinks: true, failOnError: true },
})
```

Static HTML at build time, no round-trip, and once routes are prerendered a sitemap/RSS server route is trivial to add.

**Also from the Bun migration:** your Dockerfile runs `bun ./.output/server/index.mjs`, but the build log shows `preset: node-server`. The Bun path wants `nitro({ preset: 'bun' })`. It works today, but you're not getting what you migrated for.

---

## P2 — Replace, don't upgrade

### gray-matter → anything modern

`gray-matter@4.0.3` (last published 2019) depends on `js-yaml@3`, which depends on **esprima** — a full JavaScript parser. From your build output:

```
_libs/esprima.mjs              218.47 kB
_libs/gray-matter+[...].mjs    106.80 kB
```

**325 kB of server bundle** to parse frontmatter that looks like this:

```yaml
share: true
slug: thoughts_on_module_federation_2.0
title: Thoughts on Module Federation 2.0
date: 2025-10-13
tags:
  - module federation
```

This is server-only, so it costs you image size and cold start, not user bytes — but it's the single most disproportionate thing in the dependency tree. Swap in `yaml` (eemeli) with a ~10-line splitter, and both chunks vanish.

### The `[ACTIONS: {...}]` regex is the old way to do this

`ai.functions.ts:147` asks the model to emit JSON inside a bracketed tag, then regex-extracts it. AI SDK 7 does this natively — `generateText` accepts an `output` schema (Zod/Valibot/JSON Schema) so the model returns typed structured data directly, no string parsing, no `normalizeActions` defensive layer. If you want the palette to feel live, `streamText` supports the same thing.

### Delete `sanitizeHtml`

`src/utils/markdown.ts:9` is a blocklist regex sanitizer — the category of thing that is reliably bypassable. Every input is a markdown file you wrote, committed to `src/blogs/`. **It provides no security, only the appearance of it.** Delete it. (If you ever plan to accept markdown you didn't write, that's when you reach for a real parser-based sanitizer — but don't keep this in the meantime as a placeholder.)

---

## P3 — Cheap, verified wins

I actually ran these, so the numbers are real:

- **`"strict": true` in tsconfig: zero errors.** You currently only set `strictNullChecks`. Free. Adding `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` too gives 8 errors — but 4 are in `MatrixRain.tsx`, which is dead code (see below), so it's realistically a 4-fix change.
- **`define: { global: "globalThis" }` is vestigial.** I removed it, ran a full build and the test suite — both pass. (Reverted; your tree is clean.) It's a legacy CJS shim doing blind string replacement.
- **Unused runtime dependencies:** `isbot` and `web-vitals` are in `dependencies` and imported nowhere. `baseline-browser-mapping` in devDeps likewise.
- **Dead code:** `src/constants/sentry.tsx` (a hardcoded Sentry DSN, never imported), `src/components/effects/index.ts` and `src/components/Card/index.tsx` (barrel files nothing imports — everything imports directly), `MatrixRain.tsx` (only reachable through the dead barrel), and `_isLoaded` in `routes/index.tsx:13` (set, never read).
- **Two lockfiles:** `bun.lock` and `package-lock.json`. `packageManager` says npm and the Dockerfile runs `npm ci` — `bun.lock` is a stale artifact that will drift.
- **`routes/index.tsx:16`** attaches a `mousemove` listener that calls `setMousePosition` on every event, re-rendering the entire homepage continuously while the mouse moves. A CSS custom property written through a ref does the same parallax with zero re-renders.
- **`CommandAgent.tsx:118`** mutates a ref during render (`chatHistoryRef.current = chatHistory`). React Compiler is enabled on this project and that's explicitly disallowed — and it's unnecessary, since `sendAIQuery` already has the value.
- **`CommandAgent` modal** has no `role="dialog"`, no `aria-modal`, and no focus trap; the backdrop is a full-screen `<button>` sitting in the tab order. Native `<dialog>` with `showModal()` gives you all of that for free.
- **CI:** `superfly/flyctl-actions/setup-flyctl@master` is pinned to a moving branch — pin a tag or SHA. `actions/checkout@v4` → v5.
- **Node version tells three stories:** `@types/node ^26`, `engines.node >=22.12.0`, Dockerfile `NODE_VERSION=24` — and the actual runtime is Bun 1.4, not Node. `@types/node@26` will happily type APIs that don't exist where this runs.

I'd skip syntax highlighting (Shiki) for now — you have exactly one code block across two posts.

---

## One question

Your posts have exactly two code blocks but a lot of chrome. Separately: my saved note says your design direction as of July 2026 is "refined dark minimal, single cyan accent, no cyberpunk effects" — but the code is maximum cyberpunk (`#bf00ff`, `#ff0080`, MatrixRain, scan lines, `END_OF_TRANSMISSION`, and an AI system prompt that instructs a "cyberpunk/hacker personality"). Is that note stale, or is the redesign still pending? I didn't act on it either way.

---
